key_concept: The human vertebral column has 26 vertebrae arranged from the head downward as cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1, fused) and coccygeal (1, fused).
steps: The vertebral formula of an adult human is $C_7\,T_{12}\,L_5\,S_{1}\,Co_{1}$, giving 26 vertebrae.
Cervical vertebrae (7) form the neck. They lie right below the skull, so they come first.
Thoracic vertebrae (12) come next. They form the back of the chest and articulate with the 12 pairs of ribs.
Lumbar vertebrae (5) are the large, heavy vertebrae of the lower back. They lie below the thoracic region.
The sacrum (5 fused vertebrae) lies below the lumbar region and joins the pelvic girdle. Below it is the coccyx.
So the head-to-toe order is cervical → thoracic → lumbar → sacrum, which matches option (4).
final_answer: Option (4): Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, lumbar vertebra, sacrum
why_not_others: Option (1) places the sacrum above the lumbar region, and option (3) swaps thoracic and lumbar. Option (2) gives the correct sequence but in reverse (toe to head).
common_trap: Students often pick the reversed sequence in option (2) without noticing the 'head to toe' direction, or they mix up the thoracic and lumbar positions.
time_saving_tip: Remember the formula $C_7T_{12}L_5S_1Co_1$, read top to bottom as 'C-T-L-S-Co'. Any option that begins with cervical and has the letters in this sequence is correct.
